title: Research: screen signed-ternary triple gauges of rank-34 plane fit
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Add a source-pinned exact search of latent-channel basis changes for the rank-34 P112 scalar fit in PR #3335. For each triple of its 34 channels and every rationally invertible 3x3 matrix with entries in {-1, 0, 1}, transform source columns by S and reader rows by S^-1. The scalar fitting matrix stays exactly fixed; each resulting term is priced on the complete source and reader plane spans under the inherited one-total pairing-rank tariff.

This is a scoped algebraic screen. It does not construct a physical decoder or establish a new supplier or κ.

## Result

- 19,683 signed-ternary matrices include 11,808 invertible over Q and realize 396 distinct source/inverse-reader support maps.
- All 5,984 channel triples and all 396 support maps are priced: 2,369,664 cases.
- The baseline invoice is 224. No case lowers it: 520,608 tie, and the rest cost 225 through 238.
- A determinant-2 rational control checks all 12,544 entries of the 112x112 scalar matrix; using S rather than S^-1 fails the control.

Thus one signed-ternary change of basis on any three channels does not escape the 224 full-plane invoice. This does not rule out larger blocks, arbitrary rational gauges, other scalar factorizations, or changed physical contracts.

## Validation

- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired-plane-rank34-triple-gauge` (registered normal, optimized, and focused checks; CPython 3.12.15)
- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired-plane-rank34-triple-gauge --check-only`
- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/paired-plane-rank34-triple-gauge --check-source-history`

## Task and overlap

The current orthogonal-local result already costs 224, while a favorable plane-port screen needs about 160 or less. This contribution tests the smallest nontrivial gauge that can mix those supports while preserving the exact rank-34 fit. It builds on the copy-audit handoff's open nonorthogonal cross-group question.

PR #3463 covers pair-span gauges and PR #3472 covers a common external-query perturbation; neither is this change of basis inside the fixed 34-channel factorization. The live overlap refresh paginated 703 open PRs and found no matching path or exact gauge terms. Discussion coverage was partial; #1587 and the current #1166/#1167 threads were read, and no general novelty claim is made.

## Credit

Credit Mark / Matarener for PR #3335's matching and rank-34 fit, and Arham-Tahir64 for the independent full-plane copy audit and its explicit nonorthogonal-term boundary. Their source attribution remains in the package. Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review or proof-assistant check is claimed.

## Open next questions

Use the zero-delta triples to build a support-interaction graph and screen candidate four-channel gauges before considering a larger matrix census. Any cheaper factorization still needs a complete physical decoder, dirty-state restoration, consumer, and supplier bill before it can affect κ.
